project_metadata.job_description:
Need Designer for Magazine Layout & Prepress Formatting


We are looking for someone with Magazine layout and type setting experience. We need to launch our magazine in 10 days and need it ready for physical print as well as (PDF to Digital Flip Book). The magazine will have 100 pages or less.

We will supply you the articles (Word Documents) and you need to handle the creation of the template, type setting, and layout. No graphic design from scratch is needed. 
Any advertisement pages will come to you already designed as PSD files.

***The person we hire will help us with the structure and arrangement of the magazine. 

-You will arrange provided articles (text and images) into a cohesive magazine layout.
-No original design work required; all design elements will be supplied.
-Deliver two outputs: a PDF suitable for digital flipbook use, and a print-ready version at 300 dpi.
-Magazine length: approximately 100 pages.

*The budget is $100 USD. Any bids higher, will be discarded. 

We would like to hire this person for ongoing monthly relationship.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001],

They aren’t really typos so much as punctuation inconsistencies. For instance, an en dash "–" is used where an em dash "—" should appear, and both forms are sometimes written with spaces, as in "word — word", and elsewhere without them, as in "word—word". The styling needs to remain uniform, and I would use "word — word" everywhere. For eg., the website title "Charlie Kirk – The Best and Greatest of Us" contains an en dash "–" rather than an em dash "—", so it should read "Charlie Kirk — The Best and Greatest of Us". I would also put a period after every complete sentence, including blurbs and points, because many currently omit one. One example is "Family: Married to Jeanette Dousdebes Rubio since 1998; the couple has four children". I hope that clarifies it.

Responses corresponding to your feedback:

1. The uneven empty areas at the ends of most articles aren’t solely caused by layout, font, or images. They’re mainly related to content length, since these pieces were written for the web rather than magazine editorial use. The conventional and ideal solution is to supply more text because word count is critical in magazine and newspaper editorial work. Normally, the layout is built with dummy text, "Lorem Ipsum", according to the approximate per-page word count supplied by the editorial team, and it is then balanced using images and blurbs. Once the pagination-based layout is complete, the editorial team works to the dummy text’s word count. With pre-written articles, however, the author or editorial team would shorten or expand the text to meet that count. Given our circumstances, I did as much as possible by balancing the pages with images and even adjusting text kerning. However, to achieve the same result as the "Confirmed Alien Existence Can’t Cast Doubt on Christianity' article", additional text and/or images must be added wherever possible. As an example, for "Made in the USA: The Return of Domestic Manufacturing", we could place a large image on page 24 to cover up page 25 as much as possible. Still, matching the word count by adding text is the only route to exact consistency. With that in mind, please send more images for any locations where you believe they can reduce the white space toward the end as much as possible.

2. What I sent is an optimized version, and the ads have not yet been swapped for the PSD versions you provided. All of them will be corrected in the next version.

3. If you mean the body font, it is identical to the font on your website. Nevertheless, I’ve attached 3 other options, and my choice would be the **Inter** font.

4. I provided a spread version so you could understand the layout more clearly. For Flip Book, we’ll need to upload the pages version. The total page count must be even, meaning divisible by 2. Once we’re through with this, I’ll also test it on [URL_013].

5. If the pagination order of the articles works for you, I can proceed with the Table of Contents.

At present, we need 1 ad for the blank page 99. You can still send 2-3 additional ads as backups in case they’re required.

Many thanks!

[FREELANCER_NAME_003]

A semi-condensed san serif font is strongly recommended for contemporary magazine layouts, particularly when combined with a serif heading font. Please trust me: **INTER** offers much better thickness, readability, spacing, and modern visual appeal.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Would you please add another $100 as a bonus? — surely that isn't an excessive request — you could easily spend the same amount on lunch or dinner at a restaurant. After putting my heart and soul into your product, don't I deserve that???

I absolutely want us to work as partners and build this relationship. But would that mean you'd continue paying only $100 for every monthly issue, even after you begin selling ads??? This relationship needs a roadmap that benefits both of us. At present, everything feels one-sided, and on top of that, you are asking for the source files — c'mon! It comes across as taking advantage of someone's kind and humble nature. Would you want someone to treat you like that?

Having started 3 magazines myself, I understand how this business operates. Even so, a business is normally launched with some budget — and the budget cannot be this low when the goal is to produce a high-quality niche product.

I certainly want to handle the next issue — naturally, for Stallone!!! However, we genuinely need to determine how this relationship can work over the long term.

Give it some thought, buddy. I don't need an answer immediately. Take as much time as you need.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
I understand that it may look or feel like that, but the reality is much simpler. This magazine is merely an idea with exactly what you described: 'no budget'. There is no greed or bad intention involved; this start up genuinely has no available funds. At the moment, even $20 is a substantial amount. Of course, if and when we begin selling ads, that $100 would rise to $250, $500, and so on. For now, though, we are beginning from zero.

Most importantly, both parties need to be satisfied, or it is not worthwhile. Therefore, please send me the template. I have already released the funds, and afterward I will post your feedback / review and we can continue the conversation.

Thank you!
